page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 machine family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 13.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 6.5 GB per core. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is positioned at the lower tier of absolute compute and memory throughput. The single-core stress-ng score of 1105.58 and Geekbench single-core score of 944.0 fall into the bottom 25% of tested servers, while the multi-core stress-ng score of 1452.88 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1124.0 are in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 80.89 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 11.13 GB/sec, both ranking in the bottom 10%. Static web serving throughput is measured at 1.58 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-highmem-2 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring more memory than compute power, though it trades off raw processing speed. It is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive tasks such as small database hosting, caching layers, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving where high CPU performance is not a primary requirement.
